lessons.title: From Récord to América
lessons.subtitle: A schoolyard team became a four-time champion.

story.title: A team takes shape
story.body: Students Rafael Garza Gutiérrez and Germán Núñez Cortina brought together classmates in 1916. The team took its name at a meeting in the Condesa neighborhood on October 12.

story.title: A run of titles
story.body: After returning to the name América in 1920, the club won four consecutive league championships from 1924–25 through 1927–28.

facts.prompt: In what year did the students form the team that became Club América?
facts.scope: Club origins
facts.evidence: The official club history dates the founding gathering of the team that became América to 1916.

facts.evidence: América’s official history says the team selected its name at the Condesa gathering on October 12, 1916.

facts.scope: Amateur-era league championships
facts.evidence: The official history lists four consecutive championships from 1924–25 through 1927–28.

lessons.subtitle: An unbeaten season ended with a late winner.

story.title: A perfect finish
story.body: América’s first championship came in the amateur-era 1924–25 season. The team clinched it with a narrow win over Asturias in March 1925.

story.title: A measured campaign
story.body: The club’s account records ten wins and two draws across twelve matches, with just four goals conceded.

story.body: América beat Guadalajara in the 1983–84 final to earn its eighth championship. The club describes that victory as the start of a three-title run.
